instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F. Grease a 9 by 13-inch baking dish with a little oil or nonstick spray.
Spread 1/2 cup of the marinara across the bottom of the dish.
Lay half the frozen ravioli over the sauce in one layer, overlapping them a little if you need to. Don't thaw them first.
Spoon about 1 cup of the marinara over the ravioli. Sprinkle on 1 cup of the mozzarella and half of the Italian seasoning.
Add the rest of the ravioli, then spread the remaining 1 1/2 cups marinara over them.
Sprinkle with the remaining 1 cup mozzarella, the Parmesan and the rest of the Italian seasoning.
Cover the dish tightly with foil and bake for 25 minutes.
Take off the foil and bake for 5 to 10 minutes, until the cheese is melted and golden and the sauce bubbles around the edges. Poke a ravioli with a knife. It should slide in easily.
Let the dish sit for 5 minutes before you serve it. Serve with the extra sauce from the dish spooned over each portion.

Leftovers keep for 4 days in the fridge. Warm them covered in a 350°F oven for about 20 minutes. To freeze, cool the baked dish, cover it well and freeze for up to 3 months. Thaw it in the fridge overnight before reheating.
Taste a bite. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
method_notes: None of the readable versions has 20 ratings, so this is a fallback. The lead (Family Fresh Meals, 5 from 7) layers frozen ravioli straight from the bag with marinara, mozzarella and Italian seasoning, covers the dish, and bakes it at 400°F. Spend With Pennies (5 from 7) and Kitchen Dreaming bake it at 350 to 375°F and add sausage or a cream sauce; those were left out to keep it meatless. Cover time here is 25 minutes, between the lead's 20 and Spend With Pennies' 35, because the ravioli go in frozen.
